risk.title: Risk explanation
risk.subtitle: How the score is built: every factor's contribution, compared with the student's grade cohort.
risk.totalHint: Contributions add up exactly to the score.
risk.explainer: Each factor's risk (0–100) is multiplied by its weight; factors without data are left out and the remaining weights are rescaled. “Against cohort” shows the points above (+) or below (−) a typical student in the same grade.
risk.empty: No risk score yet. It appears after the first recompute with grades or attendance.

mastery.title: Concept mastery
mastery.subtitle: Pick a class to see which concepts it is struggling with. Mastery is estimated from students' work with the AI tutor, so it only appears for concepts a student has actually practised.

noClasses.title: No classes yet
noClasses.body: This school has no classes set up, so there is nothing to show. Classes are created in the school's setup.

noStudents.title: No students in this class
noStudents.body: Nobody is enrolled in this class yet, so there is no mastery to show.

unavailable.title: Mastery is unavailable right now
unavailable.body: We can't reach the AI service that holds mastery data at the moment. Nothing has been lost — please try again a little later.

empty.title: No mastery data for this class yet
empty.body: Mastery only exists after students use the AI tutor. No student in this class has practised a concept with the tutor yet, so there is nothing to measure — this does not mean they are behind.

summary.title: Where {className} is weakest
summary.subtitle: Concepts ranked by class average, weakest first. Averages count only students who have been assessed on the concept.

grid.title: Students × concepts
grid.unassessed: {count, plural, one {# student has} other {# students have}} no tutor attempts yet.
grid.note: "No data" means not yet assessed, not zero mastery.

legend2.title: How to read the colours
legend2.body: Each cell is the estimated chance the student has mastered the concept. A dashed cell means the student hasn't attempted it yet — that is not the same as a low score, and it is left out of the class average.

aiUsage.title: AI usage and quality
aiUsage.subtitle: This school's AI spend this month against its budget, and how the evaluation suite is scoring.

unavailable.title: AI service unavailable
unavailable.body: Usage figures can't be loaded right now. Try again shortly.

nominal.title: Nominal figures — no live AI model yet
nominal.body: Every AI answer this month came from the built-in test model, not a paid provider. The spend shown is list-price arithmetic over test traffic; no money has been charged.

discretionary.name: Discretionary
discretionary.body: Tutoring, matching, essay coaching, practice and copilot. Stops at 100%; admins are warned at 80%.

essential.name: Essential
essential.body: Classification, extraction, translation and summaries — risk explanations, parent messages and translations. Never switched off by a tutor overrun.

derivation.noSeatsWhy: No student count has been reported to the AI service for this school yet, so the per-student budget ($0.10 per student a month) cannot apply yet.

hero.eyebrow: For secondary schools in Albania and the UAE
hero.title: See which students need help, and why, before the term is over.
hero.subtitle: Attendance, grades and an AI tutor in one place, so advisors act on evidence and every decision stays with a person.
hero.coverage: Albania and the UAE · Albanian, English and Arabic, with full right-to-left
hero.imageAlt: A teacher and a student working together at a laptop

proof.title: Know what a class has actually mastered
proof.body: Advisors see a class's weakest concepts first, with the class average and how many students were assessed, above a grid of every student and every concept. Mastery is estimated from students' practice with the tutor.
proof.noData: A concept nobody has attempted shows as “no data”, not zero. An untried topic and a failed one mean opposite things about a child.
proof.alt: Screenshot of the mastery heatmap for a demo class, including cells marked no data
proof.caption: A real screen from the demo school. Students and figures are synthetic.

values.title: One record, three people who need it

advisor.title: Every student who needs a decision
advisor.body: The action inbox holds every proposal the success engine makes for a student, with the risk score and the evidence behind it. A student's support track does not change until a person approves, edits or dismisses the card, and the database itself refuses anything else.
advisor.alt: Screenshot of the action inbox in the demo school

student.title: A tutor that helps, in their own language
student.body: Six ways to be helped, guiding questions by default, in Albanian, English or Arabic. When the school's AI budget for the month is spent, the tutor says so plainly. It never switches quietly to a weaker answer.

head.title: AI usage and quality, in plain figures
head.body: What was spent this month, against which cap, how that cap was worked out, and whether answer quality was actually measured. Without a live model the page says “not measured” instead of showing a pass.
items: Spend per pool against its cap
A warning to the school admin at 80%
Evaluation runs, with plumbing and answer quality reported separately

countries.title: Built for two countries
countries.body: Country differences live in data packs, not in separate products. Each pack carries the grade structure, grading scale, school calendar, consent ages and default language.

al.name: Albania
items: Two semesters, ending with the State Matura in grade 12
Marks from 4 to 10, with 5 as the pass mark
Guardian consent for online services below age 16

ae.name: United Arab Emirates
items: Three terms on the Ministry of Education calendar
A 0–100 percentage scale as the starting default

countries.confirm: Some settings, such as semester dates, grade cut-offs and consent rules, are researched starting points, not settled law. Each school confirms them for itself before relying on them.
countries.pricing: Subscribed per school. Pricing on request.

isolation.title: Each school's data is separated in the database itself
isolation.body: Row-level security in Postgres keeps one school's records invisible to every other school, underneath the application code.

disclosure.title: Disclosures go to a person
disclosure.body: If a student writes about self-harm or abuse, the message is routed to a human with no AI model involved, even when the school has switched AI off.

images.title: No images to a model
images.body: Personal details are removed before any text reaches an AI provider. Image upload in the tutor is switched off, because that filter cannot see inside a picture.

budget.title: AI spend has a hard stop
budget.body: Tutoring stops at the school's monthly limit, with a warning at 80%. Translations, summaries and risk explanations draw on a separate allowance, so a busy tutor never switches them off.

footer.demo: This is a demo, not a live service. It runs on the team's own computer with two synthetic schools, and every AI answer comes from a test stand-in because no AI provider is connected yet.
